gloss: luxury food or drink; indulgence item

definitions.gloss: luxury food or drink; indulgence item
definitions.explanation: Items consumed for pleasure rather than nutrition, such as coffee, tea, tobacco, alcohol, chocolate, and sweets. The term carries no negative judgment — it simply categorizes items enjoyed for taste or stimulation rather than sustenance.

examples.japanese: コーヒーは{代表的|だいひょうてき}な{嗜好品|しこうひん}だ。
examples.english: Coffee is a typical indulgence item.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}のために{嗜好品|しこうひん}を{控|ひか}えている。
examples.english: I'm cutting back on indulgences for my health.

examples.japanese: {嗜好品|しこうひん}にかける{費用|ひよう}を{見直|みなお}したら、{毎月|まいつき}かなり{節約|せつやく}できた。
examples.english: When I reviewed my spending on indulgence items, I was able to save quite a bit each month.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat formal category term commonly seen in health articles, nutrition guides, tax discussions, and household budgeting. The classic examples are coffee, tea, tobacco, and alcohol. Chocolate and snacks are sometimes included. The word does not imply moral judgment — it is a neutral classification.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嗜好品|しこうひん}を{控|ひか}える (to cut back on indulgences)
- {嗜好品|しこうひん}の{摂取|せっしゅ} (consumption of luxury foods/drinks)
- {嗜好品|しこうひん}{税|ぜい} (tax on luxury consumables)

NOTE ON TRANSLATION:
There is no single natural English equivalent. "Luxury grocery" is too narrow; "indulgence" is close but vague. In Japanese, the term is well-defined and commonly understood.
